stem: A client develops reproducible calf discomfort while walking that resolves after several minutes of rest. What does this pattern most strongly suggest?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis, which is characteristically relieved promptly by rest after a predictable walking distance.
options.B: Restless legs syndrome, which typically produces reproducible ischemic calf pain only during exertion.
options.C: Intermittent claudication from lower-extremity peripheral artery disease, reflecting exertional ischemia.
options.D: A normal effect of aging that does not warrant vascular assessment when symptoms resolve with rest.

rationale: NHLBI describes intermittent claudication as leg pain, aching, heaviness, or cramping that occurs during walking or stair climbing and goes away after rest; the calf is a common location. This pattern is the most common symptomatic presentation of lower-extremity PAD. C is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize reproducible exertional calf discomfort relieved by rest as intermittent claudication suggestive of lower-extremity peripheral artery disease.
source_organization: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), NIH
source_locator: PAD Symptoms: pain, aching, heaviness, or cramping in the legs that comes with walking/climbing stairs and goes away after rest is called intermittent claudication; pain is often in the calf.
source_claim_supported: Reproducible calf discomfort triggered by walking and relieved by rest is intermittent claudication and strongly suggests lower-extremity PAD.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation, printed p.14: recognize clinical manifestations and pathophysiology of acute/chronic physical-health conditions and intervene appropriately.

source_original.source_detail: PAD Symptoms — leg pain/discomfort with walking or activity that improves with rest. NHLBI page last updated 2022-03-24; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Physiological Adaptation, printed p.14: acute/chronic alterations, emergency response and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the PAD/claudication construct and key C, verified the exact NHLBI symptom pattern and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a classic presentation.

audit_findings.source_authority: NHLBI/NIH primary guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: NHLBI page last updated 2022-03-24 and live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: NHLBI PAD Symptoms intermittent claudication paragraph
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately identifies the exertion-rest pattern without claiming that symptoms alone establish PAD definitively.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because DVT is not classically a reproducible exertional-rest syndrome.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because restless legs syndrome does not produce the classic exertional ischemic pattern.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because this classic vascular symptom warrants assessment and is not a normal aging effect.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C matches the walking-provoked/rest-relieved calf pattern.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are explanations for leg symptoms and require pattern recognition.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read NHLBI PAD Symptoms/Diagnosis pages, all options, rationale and NCSBN mapping. C remained uniquely correct.
